text:
Día de los Muertos is everywhere—from Vans sneakers to Barbie dolls. But its rise in the U.S. is a recent story. 🕯️💀🌼

Learn from Rutgers University School of Communication and Information professor and author Regina Marchi about how the 1970s Chicano movement first popularized the Day of the Dead in the U.S. 🇲🇽
https://go.rutgers.edu/2nzu7k3v

Then, immerse yourself in the culture! Join the Zimmerli Art Museum, Rutgers University for Último Domingo: Día de los Muertos on Sunday, Oct. 26, from 1-3 p.m. This free event celebrates Latinx culture with art, creative activities, and interactive performances. 🪇

Join us in congratulating this Rutgers trailblazer!👇

Rutgers University has a farm. EE-I-EE-I-OH!🧑‍🌾 
What's your favorite farm animal? Let us know in the comments! 👇

Since 1864, this 100-acre gem (straddling New Brunswick and North Brunswick) has been the ultimate experiential learning lab. It’s not just a farm; it’s where thousands of future vets, agricultural researchers, and livestock experts get their start. 🐄🐖🐏

Rutgers Farm is also a beloved green escape – a slice of nature right smack in the middle of our urban campus. Next time you need a break, say hello to the pigs, sheep, goats and cows! 👋

The Garden State's bounty is truly boundless this time of year!

Disability Awareness Month is in "full swing" at Rutgers! 💃🕺
We kicked October off with a swing dance class designed just for our blind and visually impaired students. Hosted by the Rutgers Swing Club, the free tutorial paired participants with sighted partners and used voice cues and hand taps to teach them rock step in time.

Join us for these upcoming events at Rutgers:
Oct. 10 – Adaptive Sports, Health and Wellness Day (1–6 p.m., Cook/Douglas Recreation Center)
Oct. 16 – Breaking Barriers: Disability Rights & Resources for Early-Career Professionals (5:30–7:30 p.m., Alexander Library)
Oct. 21 – 4th Annual Rutgers Neurodiversity Summit (9 a.m.–4 p.m., College Avenue Student Center)
Oct. 28 – Unleashing Independence: The Vital Role of Service Dogs (2–4 p.m., Alexander Library)

Learn more about Disability Awareness Month at Rutgers: https://ow.ly/9lMW50X9cL3

Rutgers Nutritional Science majors are eating and leaving NO crumbs today! 🍽️

It's recipe trial day Rutgers School of Environmental and  Biological Sciences Teaching Kitchen, and our students are cooking up a storm. As part of Food Production and Management Rutgers Nutritional Sciences these future dietitians are crafting nutritious, delicious, and low-cost recipes for the USDA's Expanded Food and Nutrition Education Program through Rutgers Cooperative Extension.

This is a true win-win: students gain valuable hands-on experience while helping EFNEP fight nutrition insecurity. They're making magic with accessible ingredients while mastering those tough USDA guidelines.

To that, we say: "Yes, Chef!" 🧑‍🍳

Today, on #WorldTeacherDay, we celebrate all the incredible educators shaping the future – one classroom at a time!

🍎 Heide Kowalski (Camden County): Empowering sixth-grade students through English language arts at Ann A. Mullen Middle School in the Gloucester Township School District.

text: What's your favorite fall activity to do in New Jersey ?

This is what representation looks like. Say hello to Thee Scarlet Divas, Rutgers' first all-Black majorette dance team!

Since forming in 2022, they've been bringing their signature synchronized style to Black Alumni events and tailgates. But on Sept. 6, they went next level, rocking the field at SHI Stadium for the very first time alongside the Marching Scarlet Knights during halftime! 🤩
This was a huge step for visibility.

As President and co-founder Faith Jackson said, "Just being able to look up and see that we're on the jumbotron... It was exhilarating.”
Congrats to Thee Scarlet Divas! We can't wait to see this group shine for years to come. ❤️🖤

text:
How many of your classmates are parents?
The answer might surprise you. 👀
 
Most student parents at Rutgers are in graduate school, a group that, like graduate students in general, is often underacknowledged. Student parents are nearly twice as likely to drop out, and 70% struggle to afford childcare or other basic needs.
 
So, what do these incredible student parents wish you knew about the day-to-day hustle of earning a degree while raising a family?
Watch to find out. 
Rutgers Student Affairs - New Brunswick

text:
Graduate student parents: We see you! 👩‍👦
 
Juggling a graduate program with raising a family takes hard work and dedication. That's why Rutgers’ Office of Graduate Student Life is celebrating our incredible student parents during their 2nd annual #StudentParentMonth. ❤️📚
 

Graduate Student Life provides guidance, resources, and community to help student parents thrive, including:
- The office of Title IX which provides legal protections and accommodations
- The office of Basic Needs that support the food pantry/emergency aid.
- Community group connections
- On-campus family housing
 
Learn more and get connected today.🌟
